body.en:
Definition / principle

Refrigeration removes heat from a low-temperature region and rejects it at a higher temperature using supplied energy.

Understand why

Classify by method:vapour compression, vapour absorption, air/gas cycles, thermoelectric and other specialised methods.

Capacity is heat-removal rate, not the compressor electrical rating; 1 TR≈3.517kWof cooling.

A refrigerant is the working fluid; a secondary coolant such as brine carries cooling between equipment and load.

Does a higher condensing temperature usually improve COP?

No. It normally raises the required pressure lift.

h.en: 3.2.1 VCRS major components and state numbering
h.gu: 3.2.1 VCRS Major Components અને State Numbering

body.en:
Definition / principle

Use one consistent numbering convention through every diagram and equation.

Classification / types — basis first

  • Compression-refrigeration systems may be single-stage, multistage or other layouts; the syllabus basic cycle here is single-stage. VCRS has four principal functional elements:compressor, condenser, expansion device, evaporator.

Construction — each part and its purpose

  1. Compressor suction receives low-pressure vapour at state1 and discharge delivers high-pressure vapour at state2; the drive supplies work.
  2. Condenser passages expose high-pressure refrigerant to a cooler external medium, with outlet state3usually liquid.
  3. Expansion valve or capillary connects high to low pressure; its outlet state4is commonly a flashed two-phase mixture.
  4. Evaporator receives low-pressure mixture and provides a heat-transfer surface between refrigerant and the required cooled region.
  5. Refrigerant tubing closes the loop; filter-drier, receiver/accumulator where appropriate, sensors and protection support actual equipment.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. 1→2:work raises vapour pressure and enthalpy; ideal reference compression is isentropic, actual compression is not.
  2. 2→3:refrigerant first desuperheats, then condenses and may subcool while rejecting heat at approximately high-side pressure.
  3. 3→4:flow resistance causes irreversible pressure reduction with approximately unchanged enthalpy and no recovered shaft work.
  4. 4→1:refrigerant evaporates by absorbing load heat at approximately low-side pressure; controlled superheat can follow.
  5. The compressor maintains circulation and pressure separation, allowing repeated low-temperature heat removal and higher-temperature rejection.

Application / advantages

Food preservation, ice manufacture, water cooling and air-conditioning; cooling capacity is not compressor electrical rating.

Common mistake / conditions

Do not omit any of the four elements or draw an expansion turbine instead of a throttle; actual pressure drops, superheat and subcooling need the chosen property model.

Does an expansion valve recover useful shaft work?

No. In this model it throttles withh3=h4.

h.en: 3.2.2 VCR component types and their working

body.en:
Definition / principle

Each VCR component performs a specific pressure or heat-transfer duty; different constructions realise the same basic cycle functions.

Classification / types — basis first

  • Compressor principle:positive-displacement(reciprocating, rotary, scroll, screw)versus dynamic(centrifugal).
  • Condenser external cooling medium:air-cooled, water-cooled, evaporative.
  • Evaporator refrigerant feed:dry-expansion or flooded; surface/construction is a different basis, bare/finned/shell/plate as suitable.
  • Expansion control:fixed capillary, thermostatic expansion valve, electronic expansion valve and other suitable controls.

Construction — each part and its purpose

  1. A reciprocating compressor contains a cylinder, piston, crank drive, suction valve and discharge valve; scroll/screw compressors use different moving compression chambers.
  2. Air-cooled condensers expose tubes/fins to ambient air; water-cooled units separate cooling water and refrigerant by heat-transfer walls.
  3. Evaporator surfaces separate refrigerant from the useful load; finned coils suit air cooling while suitable shells/plates cool liquids.
  4. Capillary is a long narrow restriction; thermostatic expansion valves use a sensing/power arrangement, while electronic valves use an actuator/controller.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. In a reciprocating compressor, suction fills the chamber, volume reduction compresses vapour and discharge occurs when cylinder pressure exceeds discharge-side conditions.
  2. In a condenser, desuperheating and condensation transfer heat to external air/water; phase change occurs on the refrigerant side, not necessarily the cooling-water side.
  3. A capillary meters flow through pressure-dependent resistance; it has no independent active superheat sensor.
  4. Thermostatic/electronic valves modulate flow to their control objective, often suitable outlet superheat; their action is still throttling rather than useful-work expansion.
  5. In an evaporator, heat boils refrigerant; dry-expansion seeks appropriate vapour outlet, while flooded designs maintain liquid inventory using their own control arrangement.

Application / advantages

Choose component type according to capacity, temperature, load variation, available cooling medium and refrigerant approval.

Common mistake / conditions

Classification bases must remain separate; air-cooled/flooded are not opposing compressor categories. Liquid carryover into an unsuitable compressor can cause damage.

4→1:evaporation and possible superheating absorb heat at approximately constant low pressure; liquid entry to the compressor is undesirable.

body.en:
Definition / principle

COP measures useful cooling divided by supplied work; it is not a heat-engine efficiency.

Understand why

qL=h1−h4; wc=h2−h1; qH=h2−h3 in kJ/kg with negligible kinetic/potential changes.

COPR=qL/wc; QLdot=mdot qL; Wdot=mdot wc; QHdot=QLdot+Wdot.

COP can exceed1because work moves heat rather than being wholly converted into cooling energy.

CycleCOPexcludes some auxiliaries; whole-systemCOPmust state fans, pumps, controls and electrical/mechanical boundaries.

body.en:
Definition / principle

The useful load is heat entering the food compartment and heat removed from its contents.

Classification / types — basis first

  • By defrost/air circulation:direct-cool and frost-free designs; by compartment arrangement:single-door, multicompartment and other layouts. A common capillary-fed domestic VCR system is explained below.

Construction — each part and its purpose

  1. Insulated cabinet, walls and door gasket limit heat leakage; separate compartments may have different control requirements.
  2. Cabinet-side evaporator absorbs heat from food/air; fins and fan may circulate air in a frost-free design.
  3. Hermetic motor-compressor raises refrigerant pressure and is sealed to limit leakage; its suction must receive suitable vapour.
  4. Condenser at the cabinet exterior rejects heat to room air through its designed surface and airflow.
  5. Filter-drier removes suitable contaminants/moisture; capillary produces the pressure drop into the evaporator.
  6. Thermostat/electronic control, drain and any defrost heater/timer/sensors manage temperature, water and frost as applicable.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. When cooling is demanded, the compressor draws low-pressure evaporator vapour and compresses it.
  2. Hot high-pressure vapour gives heat to room air in the condenser and becomes liquid.
  3. Liquid passes through the drier and capillary; pressure reduction flashes part of the liquid.
  4. The cold mixture evaporates in the cabinet coil, absorbing heat leaking in and heat from stored contents.
  5. Vapour returns to the compressor; control cycles or modulates operation to maintain the selected conditions.
  6. In frost-free units, controlled defrost temporarily removes coil frost; fans and drain handling follow the design.

Application / advantages

Compact food preservation; insulation and suitable seals reduce continuous heat gain.

Common mistake / conditions

Door opening and warm food increase load; blocked airflow/frost reduce performance. Condenser rejects cabinet heat plus input work, so an open door does not cool the room overall.

  2. Hot high-pressure vapour condenserમાં room airને heat આપી liquid બને.
  3. Liquid drier,capillaryમાંથી જાય;pressure dropથી થોડું flash થાય.

body.en:
Definition / principle

A common block-ice plant uses refrigerant to chill brine, which cools separate water cans.

Classification / types — basis first

  • Ice manufacture includes block-ice, flake and tube-ice arrangements; this syllabus example is a conventional brine-tank BLOCK-ICE plant, not every ice-making machine.

Construction — each part and its purpose

  1. Insulated brine tank contains a secondary coolant selected to remain liquid at the operating temperature.
  2. Water cans immersed in brine hold product water separately; their walls transmit heat but prevent mixing.
  3. Evaporator coils in or coupled to the brine tank contain primary refrigerant; agitator/pump improves brine circulation.
  4. Compressor, condenser and expansion device form the primary refrigeration loop; condenser rejects plant heat.
  5. Approved handling equipment supports filling, freezing and removal of cans/blocks; water quality and hygienic separation remain essential.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. The VCR plant compresses, condenses and throttles the refrigerant to supply a low-temperature evaporator.
  2. Evaporating refrigerant removes heat from the brine; circulation spreads cooling around the cans.
  3. Water in each can first cools to its freezing point and then releases latent heat as ice forms.
  4. Further cooling of ice, if specified, adds a separate sensible-load term; heat leakage and handling add actual plant loads.
  5. The brine carries heat to the evaporator while refrigerant carries it to condenser surroundings; water, brine and refrigerant remain separate.

Application / advantages

Production of ice blocks for storage/transport duties; secondary brine distributes cooling without placing refrigerant in the product water.

Common mistake / conditions

Brine concentration, corrosion, temperature and hygiene require supervision; plant capacity alone does not set freezing time without heat-transfer details.

body.en:
Definition / principle

A drinking-water cooler removes sensible heat while protecting potable-water quality.

Classification / types — basis first

  • By water service:storage-type and instantaneous/continuous-flow; by heat rejection:air- or water-cooled condenser where designed. The explanation below uses a storage-type drinking-water cooler.

Construction — each part and its purpose

  1. Insulated potable-water tank reduces heat gain and stores cooled water; approved inlet/outlet arrangements support hygiene.
  2. Evaporator coil or separated heat exchanger cools the tank water without mixing refrigerant with drinking water.
  3. Motor-compressor circulates refrigerant; condenser and fan where applicable reject heat to surroundings.
  4. Expansion device lowers refrigerant pressure before the evaporator; filter-drier and piping protect the loop.
  5. Temperature sensor/control avoids unsuitable water temperatures; drainage and accessible cleaning provisions support safe use.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Incoming warmer water and ambient heat gain create demand in the tank.
  2. Control operates the compressor when water temperature calls for cooling.
  3. Condensed liquid refrigerant throttles and evaporates in the heat exchanger, absorbing heat from water through the separating wall.
  4. Water cools; refrigerant vapour returns to the compressor and condenser heat is released outside.
  5. Control reduces/stops cooling near the set condition; draw-off and replacement water create the next load.

Application / advantages

Useful cooling load above freezing is approximately m cp(Tin−Tout); divide by time for average capacity and include actual heat gains.

Common mistake / conditions

Water hygiene, separation and cleaning are not guaranteed merely because it is cold; instantaneous designs require a different sizing basis.

body.en:
Definition / principle

Absorption uses a refrigerant/absorbent pair and heat-driven separation rather than a large vapour compressor.

Classification / types — basis first

  • Working pair:NH3-water has NH3 refrigerant and water absorbent.
  • Working pair:water-LiBr has water refrigerant and LiBr absorbent; the refrigerant role reverses compared with ammonia-water's water role.
  • Arrangement:single-effect, multiple-effect and other absorption cycles; the following explains the basic single-effect mechanism.

Construction — each part and its purpose

  1. Evaporator removes useful cooling load; condenser rejects heat after high-pressure refrigerant vapour is generated.
  2. Absorber contacts low-pressure refrigerant vapour with absorbent solution and must reject absorption heat.
  3. Solution pump raises pressure of refrigerant-rich liquid solution, requiring far less work than compressing the corresponding vapour volume.
  4. Generator receives heat and separates refrigerant from the rich solution; purification/rectification is important in suitable ammonia-water designs.
  5. Solution pressure-reducing device returns lean solution to absorber pressure; refrigerant expansion device separately feeds evaporator.
  6. A solution heat exchanger where fitted recovers heat between hot lean and cool rich streams; it does not mix the two streams.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Evaporator vapour is absorbed at low pressure; cooling water/air removes the released absorption heat.
  2. Pump raises the pressure of refrigerant-rich solution and sends it towards the generator, possibly through a heat exchanger.
  3. Generator heat releases high-pressure refrigerant vapour; the solution left behind is leaner in refrigerant.
  4. Refrigerant condenses, rejects heat, throttles and evaporates to complete its primary cooling circuit.
  5. Lean solution returns through its separate pressure-reduction path and absorbs more vapour, closing the solution circuit.
  6. Generator heat plus pump work must be counted in performance; small pump work does not mean free cooling.

Application / advantages

Uses suitable waste/process/solar heat when available; low mechanical work and quiet liquid pumping can be useful.

Common mistake / conditions

LiBr-water needs above-freezing water-refrigerant service with vacuum/crystallisation control; NH3-water needs toxicity/material/purification controls. COP basis differs from electric VCR.

Definition / Principle

Absorptionમાં refrigerant/absorbent pair,heat-driven separation હોય,મોટો vapour compressor નહિ.

Classification / Types — પહેલાં Basis

  • Working pair:NH3-waterમાં NH3 refrigerant,water absorbent.
  • Working pair:water-LiBrમાં water refrigerant,LiBr absorbent;ammonia-waterની water roleથી જુદી.

  2. Absorber low-pressure vapourને solution સાથે contact કરાવે,absorption heat reject કરે.
  3. Solution pump refrigerant-rich liquid pressure વધારે;corresponding vapour compression કરતાં ઘણું ઓછું work.
  4. Generator heatથી rich solutionમાંથી refrigerant છૂટું કરે;suitable ammonia-waterમાં purification/rectification મહત્વનું.

  1. Low pressureએ vapour absorb થાય;cooling water/air absorption heat દૂર કરે.
  2. Pump rich solution pressure વધારી possible exchangerથી generator તરફ મોકલે.
  3. Generator heatથી high-pressure vapour છૂટે;બાકી solution refrigerantમાં lean થાય.
  4. Refrigerant condense,heat reject,throttle,evaporate થઈ primary cooling circuit પૂરી કરે.
  5. Lean solution separate pressure-reductionથી પાછું,વધુ vapour absorb કરી solution circuit પૂરી કરે.
  6. Performanceમાં generator heat,pump work બન્ને;small pump work એટલે free cooling નહિ.

Application / લાભ

Definition / principle

Low-pressure evaporator vapour enters the absorber; absorption releases heat that must be rejected.

The refrigerant-rich solution is pumped to generator pressure; heat releases refrigerant vapour and leaves a refrigerant-lean solution.

The lean solution returns through pressure reduction; refrigerant vapour condenses, throttles and evaporates to complete its loop.
